title: observability: token-level cost/latency dashboard + alert tuning + tracing enrichments
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: provide token-level observability (latency/cost) end-to-end to reduce perf/regression debugging time and to tune noisy alerts. This PR introduces: 1) new Prometheus/exporter metrics for token emission latency and per-token cost units, 2) enriched tracing spans with token offsets and sampling keys, 3) Grafana dashboard with token-level breakdowns, and 4) alert tuning to reduce noise while keeping SLO guardrails. Checklist: - [x] Add metric names and instrumentation in serving runtime - [x] Add tracing span attributes at token emission points - [x] Add Prometheus scrape config + exporter adjustments - [x] New Grafana dashboard panels (cost-per-token, p50/p90/p99 token emit latencies, token KV-cache hit rates) - [x] Alert rule changes (reduced sensitivity for non-user-facing latencies, added anomaly suppression during canary) - [x] Unit + integration tests for new metrics endpoints - [x] Docs + runbook updates (console + ops runbook) Implementation notes and context: we observed multiple incidents where tail token emission latency caused request-level SLO violations but root cause was upstream KV-cache churn or oversized batching. Existing metrics were at request-level and obscured token-level tails. This PR adds two primary metrics: redwood_token_emit_latency_seconds (histogram) and redwood_token_cost_units_total (counter), plus redwood_token_kv_cache_hit_ratio (gauge). Tracing now attaches token_offset and token_phase attributes to the token_emit span to help correlate with kernel-level stalls. Grafana dashboard includes: token latency heatmap per model, per-route cost breakdown, percentiles over sliding windows, and an aggregate cost-per-100k-tokens chart for billing visibility. Alert tuning: lowered alert sensitivity on request_total_latency when token-level tail is not present, added a token-latency-based alert (p99 > 120ms sustained for 10m) with a higher severity, and suppressed alerts for canary deployments via label filtering. Backwards compatibility: all new metrics are additive and default scrape retention is unchanged.

review_comments: Marta Lopez: Can you confirm the histogram bucket choices cover up to 1s? We saw kernel stalls that spiked to ~800ms in perf-canary. - Reply (author): Buckets updated after perf run; they include 1ms..1s exponential buckets and an overflow. Added comment in code explaining rationale.

Samir Patel: The new token-level metric cardinality looks safe but we should ensure label explosion doesn't occur for per-route model variants. Suggest adding route whitelisting. - Reply (author): Added route whitelist config in prometheus_exporter with sane defaults (top 50 routes) and documented how to opt-in more routes.

Jordan Kim: Alert rule change reduces sensitivity, but how do we ensure we don't silently miss regressions? Suggest adding a higher-severity token-p99 alert. - Reply (author): Added token-p99 sustained alert (p99 > 120ms for 10m) as major; kept request-level alerts as warning-level when token signals are absent.
Marta Lopez: Small nit: update the dashboard README with how to interpret token cost-per-100k chart. - Reply (author): Done; added interpretation notes and example queries.
CI Bot: grafana schema validation failed on first run (panel ref missing). - Reply (author): Fixed panel ref and added CI validation script to avoid regressions.
